gin-divergence-realtextGINMEASUREDLINKED STALE2026-07-05On six two-node queries over excerpts of public institutional and advocacy texts, the no-continuation arm kept both sides of each divergence and fabricated nothing, with Mistral-7B and with Qwen2.5-7B.Generality. gin-nc-baselineGINMEASUREDLINKED STALE2026-07-02On a 20-query synthetic eval set, SEAR's no-continuation arm produced no fabricated claims, while a plain RAG arm on the same set fabricated about a quarter of its claims.Performance on real-world corpora (this set is synthetic and author-built). gin-bookkeeperGINBUILTLINKED 2026-10-04The Bookkeeper is the single admission gate for GIN's graph state: it checks a confidence floor, endpoint existence, self-loops, anchor integrity, duplicates and DAG acyclicity, then stamps provenance on what it admits.Any measurement of the Bookkeeper. gin-sear-decode-constraintGINBUILTLINKED 2026-10-04GIN's SEAR layer constrains every generated token, at decode time, to continue a span that occurs verbatim in the retrieved corpus, using a custom llama-cpp-python logits processor.That the constrained output is correct or fair to its source. gin-encoder-sweepGINNEGATIVE-RESULTLINKED STALE2026-07-25Frozen sentence-embedding geometry did not separate issue-framing divergence: five encoders, including an NLI-trained one, each recovered 0 of 4 issue_frame pairs.That no learned method can detect framing. gin-judge-capabilityGINNEGATIVE-RESULTLINKED STALE2026-07-13A bigger LLM judge did not detect issue-framing contradictions better: recall on the 4 gold pairs went 2, 1, 2, then 0 across Mistral-7B, a Qwen 14B MoE, Qwen2.5-14B and a frontier model.That framing is undetectable. The README's own reading is that the frontier judge read the pairs as corroborating or unrelated and disagreed with the gold, so the 'contradicts' label is a contestable curatorial stance. Four gold pairs cannot separate 'judge is weak' from 'label is arguable'.

latch-pilot-killedLatchKILLEDLINKED 2026-11-11The Latch pilot, a typed-operator admission gate against free chain-of-thought on multi-hop QA, was killed at its preregistered G3 gate: the gated arm scored 37.5% at full coverage against 80.6% for chain-of-thought.Anything about gates that anchor to literal artifacts (fetched bytes, export rows). It tests a model translating a free-form question into a formal schema. Scoring was manual and not blinded; few-shot Example 5 was written from errors in the same 72 questions, which makes Arm 2's number optimistic; and PREREG section 5 treats abstentions as 'not answered, never wrong' while the headline scores them as wrong.
